Answer: B
Reason: The clinical presentation of chest pain and neck swelling after an alcoholic binge (suggesting vomiting/retching) is classic for spontaneous pneumomediastinum (Hamman's syndrome), caused by alveolar rupture due to increased intrathoracic pressure. While the provided image appears relatively normal or subtle, this diagnosis best fits the specific history and symptoms described compared to the other options which imply more severe pathology (esophageal rupture, mediastinitis) or incorrect mechanisms.
